title: Affordable novel device (VY) for transperineal prostate biopsy: A trial on prostate mannequin
author: Pramod, Safriadi, et al.

steps.title: Prepare prostate mannequin
steps.instruction: Create a custom prostate mannequin by mixing gelatin, glycerin, sorbitol, and psyllium, embedding a balloon filled with a gelatin mold shaped like the prostate, and randomly placing a mulberry target of approximately 1–1.5 cm³ inside the prostate region.

substeps.instruction: Mix gelatin, glycerin, sorbitol, and psyllium to form a homogeneous matrix.
Prepare a balloon and fill it with a gelatin mold that mimics prostate anatomy.
Place the balloon within the gelatin‑based matrix to serve as the biopsy target.
Insert a mulberry of size ~1–1.5 cm³ randomly into the prostate area of the mannequin.

steps.title: Train residents on VY device
steps.instruction: Provide standardized training on the operation of the VY transperineal biopsy device to first‑year urology residents.

steps.title: Randomize resident groups
steps.instruction: Randomly assign the twenty residents into two groups of ten: Group A performs the VY technique first then the fan technique; Group B performs the fan technique first then the VY technique.

steps.title: Perform VY transperineal biopsy
steps.instruction: Using the VY device, each resident conducts a transperineal prostate biopsy on the mannequin according to the device’s standard operating procedure.

steps.title: Perform fan‑technique biopsy
steps.instruction: Conduct a transperineal prostate biopsy on the mannequin using the fan technique with a PAJUNK® biopsy gun, an 18 G biopsy needle, an 18 G IV catheter, and transrectal ultrasonography, without any needle‑guiding tools.

substeps.instruction: Set up the PAJUNK® biopsy gun.
Attach an 18 G biopsy needle to the gun.
Insert an 18 G IV catheter as needed for the procedure.
Use transrectal ultrasonography to locate the target within the mannequin.
Advance the needle to the target and fire the biopsy gun, performing the biopsy without a needle guide.
